sec1.titulo: Before you hear any of it
abertura: In class you will join a call that is already running: the same group, the Thursday check-in, and the professor has answered at last.
Mark the three statements that are true of a call you join late.

itens.t: The most important thing is usually said fast, and only once.
itens.porque: Yes. Times and numbers are said in passing, because the person saying them already knows them.

itens.t: If you wait until the end, someone will summarize it for you.
itens.porque: No. At the end everyone leaves. The summary is the thing you have to ask for while they are still talking.

itens.t: Asking someone to repeat a number makes you look like you were not listening.
itens.porque: No. It is the opposite: the person asking is the one who is following. The person who says nothing may not be.

itens.t: You can come into a conversation without being invited.
itens.porque: Yes, and on a call you have to, because nobody can see you waiting.

itens.t: Saying back what you understood is a good way to find out you were wrong.
itens.porque: Yes, and it is cheap: one sentence now instead of the wrong section on Saturday night.

itens.t: Understanding every word is what makes a call go well.
itens.porque: No. You will not get every word, at this speed, in a second language. What matters is what you do at the moment you lose it.

sec1.rationale: A call you joined late is not a test of understanding. It is a test of what you do in the two seconds after you stop understanding: wait, or ask.

nota.titulo: Why this one is harder than the reading
nota.texto: The chat waited for you. The call does not. You cannot scroll back, you cannot reread, and the two people talking are both older than you and know each other better. That is exactly why the six expressions below exist.

abertura: Choose the better reading for each expression. All six are for interrupting, and none of them is rude.

itens.t: Can I jump in?
alts: I am coming in now, politely
I am asking permission and waiting for an answer
itens.ok: I am coming in now, politely

itens.t: Sorry, can you go back to…?
alts: I am naming the part I lost
I am apologizing for not understanding
itens.ok: I am naming the part I lost

itens.t: Wait, which one are we doing?
alts: I disagree with the plan
I heard two options and I need one
itens.ok: I heard two options and I need one

itens.t: Just to check I got that…
alts: I am saying it back so they can correct me
I am asking them to explain it again from the start
itens.ok: I am saying it back so they can correct me

itens.t: Say that again?
alts: Formal, for a long explanation
Short, informal, for one word or one number
itens.ok: Short, informal, for one word or one number

itens.t: Before you move on —
alts: I am ending the conversation
I am stopping them at the right second
itens.ok: I am stopping them at the right second

nota.titulo: Three words, and the call stops
nota.texto: Say that again? will feel too short to you. It is not. Between people your age, a long apology before a question is what sounds strange — it makes a two-second repair into a small event.

abertura: These lines come from the call you will hear. What is each one giving you?
opcoes: a rule about how they work

itens.t: “She wants one detail. One.”
itens.porque: The biggest change in the call: the presentation is no longer about the painting, it is about one small part of it.

itens.t: “Upload by Saturday, nine at night.”
itens.porque: A time, and it is earlier than the group thought. It is said once, in the middle of a sentence about something else.

itens.t: “It is twelve minutes now, not fifteen.”
itens.porque: A change, and it decides how long every section can be. Three minutes is a whole section.

itens.t: “Do not send the file in the chat. Put it in the folder.”
itens.ok: a rule about how they work
itens.porque: A rule, with a reason behind it: last time two versions went around and the wrong one was presented.

itens.t: “She asked us a question and nobody has answered it.”
itens.porque: The same unclaimed email from last week, and now it has grown: there is a question in it, from the person marking the work.

itens.t: “We need someone on the context section.”
itens.porque: The second job, and it comes with your name attached, because you are the one who just joined.

nota.titulo: What gets missed on a call
nota.texto: Not the arguments. The arguments are long and repeated. What gets missed is a number, a time, and a small change of plan, because each one is said in three words by someone who already knew it.

sec4.titulo: When it is worth stopping them
abertura: You can only interrupt so many times before it slows the call down. Mark the three moments that are worth it.

itens.t: You did not catch a time or a date.
itens.porque: Yes. A wrong time costs the whole group, and it takes four words to fix.

itens.t: You heard two options and you do not know which one was chosen.
itens.porque: Yes. This is the one that sends people away doing different things.

itens.t: You did not understand one word, and the sentence still made sense.
itens.porque: No. Let it go. You can ask afterwards, and most of the time you will not need to.

itens.t: You are about to be given a job and you are not sure what it involves.
itens.porque: Yes, and before you accept it, not after. Afterwards it sounds like you are backing out.

itens.t: Somebody used an expression you liked and want to remember.
itens.porque: No, not in the middle of a call. Write it down and ask your teacher.

itens.t: You disagree with something, but the group has moved on.
itens.porque: Not here. That is a different move, and it needs more room than a repair does.

sec4.rationale: Interrupt for what will change what you do next: a time, a choice between two things, or a job you are about to be given. Everything else can wait.

nota.texto: On a fifteen-minute call you have room for two or three repairs before people start talking around you. Spending them on the time and the change of plan is what an experienced listener does.

abertura: Each opening needs the missing piece named. Choose the version that actually gets it back.

nota.titulo: Name the piece, or they choose for you
nota.texto: Can you go back? makes the other person decide what you missed, and they will go back to whatever THEY thought was important. Can you go back to the part about the folder? gets you the folder.

nota.titulo: Six lines is the whole lesson
nota.texto: Nothing here explains anything or gives an opinion. Six short interruptions, and you come off that call knowing the time, the change and the job you took. That is what you are practicing.

itens.t: The presentation is twelve minutes long.
itens.porque: Said, once, at the end of a long sentence: twelve now, not fifteen, because a fourth group was added.

itens.t: The slides have to be uploaded on Saturday night.
itens.porque: Said, with the hour: nine at night, so Priya can look at it on Sunday morning.

itens.t: The group has presented the wrong version of a file before.
itens.porque: Said by Nate, as the reason for the folder rule. It is the kind of detail that sounds like background and is actually an instruction.

itens.t: Nate is annoyed that the time was cut.
itens.porque: Implied. It said fifteen on the sheet she sent in June is a complaint wearing the clothes of a fact.

itens.t: Priya does not trust the group to finish on time.
itens.porque: Implied. She wants the file the night before so she can check it herself, which tells you what she expects.

itens.t: Professor Okafor approved the choice of the painting.
itens.porque: Never said. She changed what the presentation is about; nobody on the call says a word about whether she liked the Vermeer.

cl2.prompt: Which of these gets the missing piece back -- and which one leaves you where you were?

itens.t: “Sorry, I didn’t catch all of that.”
itens.porque: No. It tells them you missed something and leaves them to guess which part. They will repeat what mattered to them.

itens.t: “Wait — twelve minutes, or fifteen?”
itens.porque: Yes. It names the exact thing that is unclear, and it can be answered in one word.

itens.t: “Could you possibly repeat what you were explaining?”
itens.porque: No, twice over: it does not say which part, and on a call between three people it sounds like a different kind of English from everyone else’s.

itens.t: “Just to check I got that: the file goes up Saturday at nine.”
itens.porque: Yes. It says the piece back, so they confirm it or correct it, and you leave the call certain.

cl2.rationale: A repair that works names the missing piece. A repair that does not hands the choice back to the person talking, and they repeat whatever they thought was important.

abertura: A quick reference to the call and the language you used.

tabela: A group call already running, with a change of plan, a new time and two unclaimed jobs in it.
Coming in uninvited, getting one thing repeated and confirming another.

callout.titulo: The one that changes the most
callout.texto: Just to check I got that… is the only one that makes the other person confirm or correct you. Everything else gets you information; this one tells you whether the information you have is right.

abertura: Record a short voice message, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
Think of a conversation this week that went too fast for you — in English or not: a class, a call, a group of people talking over each other.

What you are trying to do: say what you missed, what you would ask for now, and what you would say to check you had understood.

The whole C1 index: meetings, lectures, phone calls. Pick the ones where more than one person is speaking, which is the hard kind.

abertura: Two talks about listening, from people who do it for a living.

itens.texto: A sound expert on why we stop listening and how to get it back. Listen for RASA, near the end — the third letter is what you practiced today.

itens.titulo: Finding the story inside the painting
itens.texto: A novelist on standing in front of one painting until it gives you something to say. It is exactly the job your group now has: one detail, twelve minutes.
